findings.evidence: Lines 263 and 280 declare the only two restriction theorems `private`; grep finds no public alternatives.
findings.fix: Expose `isAnalyticContinuationAlong_comp_half_left` and `_right` (with suitable public names and documentation).
findings.issue: Both factor-restriction results are private, so users cannot turn a continuation along `p.trans q` into continuations along `p` and `q`, despite this being a stated product of the module.

findings.evidence: Lines 159 and 164 reduce `transFamily` to `F` or `G` under disjoint comparison hypotheses and strictly eliminate the definition, so they are terminating normal-form rules; only the endpoint lemmas currently carry `[simp]`.
findings.issue: The characteristic first- and second-half equations for `transFamily` are not `[simp]`, forcing consumers to unfold or manually rewrite the piecewise definition.

summary: The concatenation API omits its advertised restriction direction and lacks automation on its piecewise normal forms.
